title: Human Risk Graph organization
description: People and the dependencies between them, as read by `hrg analyze`. Unique IDs and references to existing people are checked by the tool itself.

$schema.description: Schema reference for editor support; ignored by the tool.

coverage.description: Written by hrg scan: where the data comes from and what could not be seen.

review_required.description: Whether the branch requires approving reviews; unknown when not visible.

gaps.description: Data the scan could not see; shown in every report.

repositories.description: Repositories an organization scan (hrg scan github --org) covered.

people.description: Everyone who takes part in approvals, escalations or bypasses.

id.description: Unique identifier, referenced by dependencies. Quote it in YAML if it looks like a number or a boolean.

criticality.description: How important the person is for security-relevant work, from 0 to 1. People at 0.7 or above are treated as critical.

last_active.description: When the person was last seen active, as an ISO date such as 2026-03-01, or "never" when a scan found no activity. Model hrg-3 reports performers inactive for longer than inactive-days (HRG007). Without it, activity is unknown and not reported.

functions.description: Critical functions for model hrg-3 (experimental): what the organization must be able to do and who can do it.

criticality.description: How much the organization depends on the function.

requires.description: People needed to complete it; 2 for a two-person rule.

performers.description: Person IDs who are trained and authorized to perform it.

alone.description: Person IDs who can complete it without the others, despite requires.

separation.description: required: one person completing it alone is a risk (segregation of duties). not-required: completing it alone is the intended policy, for example a restore by the on-call engineer; it is left out of solo control and HRG006.

from.description: Source person ID. Approval authority is counted for this person.

type.description: Kind of dependency. approval, escalation and bypass drive the metrics; other values are kept but not scored.

weight.description: Strength of the dependency, from 0 to 1.

review.description: For bypasses: 'after' if every use is reviewed afterwards (break-glass). Counted at half weight in override exposure.

source.description: Where the dependency comes from, e.g. pr-reviews, codeowners, branch-rules (set by hrg scan).

confirmed.description: false until a person has checked the dependency; reports count unconfirmed ones.
